config.detail: Branch large_ctc (the repo's main branch is the 220M ctc model). Hydra-style config under cfg.model.cfg: same encoder classes as gigaam-v3 at 24 layers, d_model=1024, 16 heads; head=CTCHead with feat_in=1024, num_classes=71 (70 chars + 1 blank). decoding=CTCGreedyDecoding with an inline character vocabulary. model_name=multilingual_large_ctc; model_class=ctc.

preprocessor.detail: Frontend declared inside config.json under cfg.model.cfg.preprocessor (features=64, n_fft=320, hop=160, win=320, center=false). Unlike the v3 configs it does not list mel_scale / mel_norm; gigaam's FeatureExtractor never passes them to torchaudio, so the frontend is the same HTK, unnormalized filterbank as v3.

tokenizer_config.detail: Charwise tokenizer; vocabulary is inline in config.json under cfg.model.cfg.decoding.vocabulary: 70 strings (space, apostrophe, a-z, 33 Russian letters including ё, and і ғ қ ң ү ұ һ ә ө for Kazakh, Kyrgyz and Uzbek Cyrillic).

tokenizer_model.detail: Branch has no tokenizer.model file: `Tokenizer.charwise=True` path, as in gigaam-v3-ctc.

generation_config.detail: Decoding is CTC greedy; no HF generation_config.

model_weights.detail: PyTorch pickle, 2,341,592,643 bytes, LFS sha256 c3fabefb50b41f08f4d7ad44e02c26c37d242882704cdcca2ebd98e45eff73d1. All tensors float32, every key prefixed `model.` by the HF wrapper.

safetensors_metadata.detail: Repo ships PyTorch pickle, not safetensors.

model_card.detail: One card covers the ssl, ctc, large_ssl and large_ctc branches; WER table on Common Voice, FLEURS and internal sets for ru, en, kk, ky, uz.

reference_modeling_code.path: https://github.com/salute-developers/GigaAM (gigaam package classes, built from the HF snapshot by scripts/lib/gigaam_hf.py)
reference_modeling_code.detail: Author-first PyTorch implementation, MIT. The pinned package commit 6e4b027c predates gigaam.load_model('multilingual_large_ctc') (added in 559d88d), but its preprocessor, ConformerEncoder, CTCHead and CTCGreedyDecoding already cover this config; the commits from 6e4b027c to 7447938 change the encoder only for padded batch inputs. The HF repo also ships modeling_gigaam.py with the same classes.

key_fields.tokenizer.vocab_inline: 70 entries: space, apostrophe, a-z, а-я, ё, і, ғ, қ, ң, ү, ұ, һ, ә, ө.

reference_rationale: Same as the rest of the gigaam family: the salute-developers `gigaam` package (MIT) at the family pin 6e4b027c. Its classes are instantiated from the pinned HF snapshot (config.json + pytorch_model.bin at large_ctc 3905cd51) by scripts/lib/gigaam_hf.py, because the package's own download for this variant needs a newer package and a CDN that the family does not pin.
known_risks: Encoder is the gigaam-v3 Conformer at 24 layers, d_model=1024; the C++ graph reads both from GGUF KV and has only been validated at 16 x 768 before this variant.
CTCHead is `nn.Conv1d(1024, num_classes=71, kernel_size=1)` + `log_softmax(-1)`. Blank id = 70 = num_classes - 1, appended after the inline vocab.
Charwise tokenizer: the inline vocab order is the CTC class order; the converter must keep it, including the non-ASCII Kazakh / Kyrgyz / Uzbek letters, and must not sort or deduplicate.
No language input and no language-detection output: the model picks characters from all five languages' alphabets per frame, so a --language hint has no effect on decoding.
Conv1d subsampling, SpecScaler log, center=false, HTK mel without area normalization, rotary attention: same gotchas as gigaam-v3.
Upstream evaluates WER on lowercased, punctuation-free text with numerals spelled out; the model emits no digits, casing or punctuation, so WER comparisons need the same normalization.
Only the ru golden case is in the manifest; numerical parity for the other four languages rests on the shared graph and is not dumped.

intake_gaps.reason: Published scores are context only. The Oracle reference WER baseline (Stage 2 Step 7) and the per-language WER sweep (Stage 7) have not been run for this variant.
Converter emits every tensor at F32 (reference dtype); same as the v3 variants.
